intro.title: How it works
intro.zh1: Chinese is written in characters: each one is said as one syllable and carries a meaning. A word like 爸爸 (bàba, dad) has two.
intro.zh2: Pinyin writes the sound in Latin letters. Its accents are the tones: ā stays high, á rises, ǎ dips then rises, à falls.
intro.zh3: Each new word is shown to you first, drawn stroke by stroke, with its meaning and pinyin. Then you recognise it, then you write it.
intro.kana1: Kana write sounds, like an alphabet: each sign is a syllable (か reads ka).
intro.kana2: Hiragana write Japanese words, katakana write words from other languages.
intro.kana3: Each new sign is shown to you first, drawn stroke by stroke, with its reading. Then you read it, then you write it in stroke order.
intro.kanji1: A kanji carries a meaning: 水 means water.
intro.kanji2: It often has two readings: on, from Chinese and written in capitals (SUI), and kun, Japanese (mizu).
intro.kanji3: Each new kanji is shown to you first, drawn stroke by stroke, with its meaning and readings. Then you recognise it, then you write it.
